title: a ticket says who wrote it and through which door
intention: a ticket says who wrote it and through which door
what: A ticket records WHO WROTE IT and THROUGH WHICH DOOR, as two required fields the /sorted door refuses to let go silent — so the corpus can answer 'who made this' now, and can still answer it when the fleet stops being one.
why: The corpus cannot say who made it. 263 tickets exist and every one was written by a hand — CC's — at Akien's direction, through /sorted; and no field records that, which is how a false claim ('nothing in Cairn has ever written a ticket') stood for a day with nothing in the corpus able to contradict it. `owner` answers a different question (who gates writes) and `cast_by` tried to answer this one and drifted into two vocabularies before going quiet. The lived symptom is Akien's: he has never written a ticket, there are hundreds of them, and the record does not say where they came from. It gets worse rather than better the moment a second writer exists.
how: MEASURED over all 263 tickets: `owner` on 257 (97%) but it is a GOVERNANCE field — who gates writes — carried as free prose in ~42 distinct phrasings, and it never answers who wrote the thing. `cast_by` on 39 (14%) and it is CONFLATED: 10 say `CC` and 9 say `/sorted`, a who and a through-what under one key. `author` on 17 (6%). `created_by` and `by` on zero. So: (1) add `author` — the hand or agent that wrote it (CC, Akien, codemother, aider), and `via` — the door it came through (/sorted, direct, imported); (2) make the /sorted door REQUIRE author, the way it already requires title, so a silent one is refused rather than defaulted; (3) migrate the 263 — and the migration is the interesting part, because it must not guess. A ticket carrying a sorted_berth was written by whoever fired that berth and the berth says so; a ticket with no berth predates the door and its author is recoverable from git blame on the file's first commit. Where neither resolves, the field says so explicitly rather than defaulting to CC. (4) `cast_by` is not deleted — it is read once during migration and then retired, with its two meanings split into the two fields that should have held them. DO NOT add a third field for whose direction it was: `from_idea` already carries that when the idea is Akien's, and a fourth field nobody fills is worse than three that are.
traces_to: Law 6 — everything has exactly one owner, and a corpus that cannot say who authored a record cannot route a correction back to the hand that made it. Law 7 — a ticket is a record of truth and an unattributed record cannot be checked against its author's standing. And Law 10, in the direction that bit today: authorship is measurable, has never been measured, and 'nothing writes tickets' passed unchallenged for a day precisely because no field held the counter-evidence.
falsifier: DONE when every ticket in the corpus carries a resolvable `author` and `via`; when the /sorted door refuses a cast with no author; and when the question 'who wrote this ticket' is answered by reading one field rather than by inference. HORIZON: the migration's own count — 263 of 263, with the unresolvable ones saying why rather than defaulting. WRONG INTENT if the fields land and everything reads `CC` forever, because then it is a constant wearing a field's clothes and the corpus is no better off than `owner` is today — the reading that matters is the DISTINCT VALUE COUNT once a second author exists, not the presence of the key.
children: none, because the field, the door check and the migration are one seam over one store. The migration is not a separable child — a field added without migrating the 263 leaves the corpus in two shapes, which is worse than either shape alone.

watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier: tickets carrying author, tickets carrying via, distinct author values, distinct via values, and the count of unresolvable-and-saying-so
watchme.consumer: whoever routes a correction back to the hand that made a ticket, and Akien, who asked the question that cast this
watchme.enough: DELIBERATELY NOT SATISFIABLE BY PRESENCE. The watch clears only when the corpus holds at least 2 DISTINCT author values across at least 20 tickets — because the failure this ticket names is a field that reads CC forever, which presence alone cannot distinguish from a field nobody thought about. Until a second writer exists the watch stands open and SAYS SO, reporting the distinct-value count rather than clearing green on 263/263 populated. This is the ticket's own falsifier honoured rather than rounded off.
watchme.nexus: the tickets store's tree — the corpus's own record of who makes it
watchme.trigger: each ticket cast through the /sorted door, plus a corpus sweep at each build_inspector run

out: A third field for whose direction it was. `from_idea` already carries that when the idea is Akien's, and a fourth field nobody fills is worse than three that are.

Reshaping `owner`. It is on 97% of tickets in ~42 phrasings and it answers a different question (Law 6 governance). Tidying it is real work and it is not this work; conflating the two is how cast_by died.
Multi-valued / joint authorship. Named as the standing assumption, deliberately unbuilt — the fleet is one, and building for an imagined population is the reflex this system keeps catching.

Defaulting an unresolvable author to CC. Explicitly forbidden: a corpus reading CC everywhere is indistinguishable from one never migrated, and would be a false green over the exact question the field exists to answer.

open_for_akien:
Two, and both are spec choices rather than measurements. (1) Should `via` be a CLOSED vocabulary in the store charter (/sorted, direct, imported) or a free string? Closed stops the ~42-phrasing drift that happened to `owner`; free costs nothing today. My read: closed, because the drift is measured and not hypothetical. (2) Does `author` name the AGENT (CC) or the SESSION (akiendelllinux_cc_0), which is what 9 tickets' `owner` values already use? My read: the agent, with the session recoverable from the sorted_berth — but the two are genuinely different answers to 'who' and it is your call which one the corpus should be able to sort by.

ANSWERED FROM THE CORPUS (CC, 2026-09-09, Fable pass over Opus's open questions — spec choices left standing for Akien to overrule): (1) `via` is a CLOSED vocabulary and compares through cairn.tools.system_word — that is the 2026-09-07 ruling 'any word he could type folds case; free text never folds' applied to a field the door reads, and the `owner` drift (~42 phrasings) is the measured cost of leaving it free. (2) `author` names the AGENT (CC | Akien); the session is recoverable from `sorted_berth`, which already carries the firing that cast the ticket, so storing it twice would be a second copy of one measurement. Both settle by an existing ruling or an existing field, so neither needs to wait at his gate; he overrules by saying so.
